name: Baby Registry Checklist
description: What to add to your baby registry, organized by category.

items.text: Register for a crib or bassinet that meets current safety standards
Add a firm, well-fitting crib mattress
Include three or four fitted crib sheets
Add a few wearable blankets or sleep sacks in newborn size
items.note: Skip loose blankets, pillows, and bumpers for the sleep space.

items.text: Register for a baby monitor that fits your home
Add blackout curtains and a small night light
Register for bottles in a couple of sizes to see what your baby prefers
Add a bottle brush and a drying rack
Include burp cloths, at least eight to ten
Register for a nursing pillow if you plan to breastfeed
Add a breast pump and storage bags if pumping is part of your plan
items.note: Check your insurance, as a pump may be covered.

items.text: Include several bibs for the early months
Add a few cans or supply of formula if you plan to use it
Register for newborn and size 1 diapers in a few packs
Add fragrance-free wipes in bulk
Include a changing pad with a washable cover
Register for a diaper pail or sealed trash system
Add diaper cream and a small basket to keep supplies handy
Include a portable changing kit for the diaper bag
Register for short- and long-sleeve onesies in 0 to 3 and 3 to 6 months
Add footed sleepers with easy snaps or zippers
Include socks, hats, and scratch mittens
Add seasonally appropriate layers like a sweater or bunting
Register for a few swaddle blankets
Include extra burp cloths and washcloths
Register for an infant car seat that fits your vehicle
Add a stroller, or a travel system that pairs with the car seat
Include a baby carrier or wrap
Register for a roomy, washable diaper bag
Add a portable play yard for naps away from home
Register for a baby bathtub or a sink insert
Add hooded towels and soft washcloths
Include fragrance-free baby wash and lotion
Add a soft hairbrush and baby nail clippers or a file
Include a digital thermometer
items.note: Ask your pediatrician which type they recommend for a newborn.

items.text: Register for outlet covers and cabinet latches for later use
Add a baby gate if you have stairs
Include a nasal aspirator for stuffy noses
Register for a basic baby first aid kit
Add a humidifier for dry-air seasons
Include a fitted, breathable mattress protector

faq.q: When should I start my baby registry?
faq.a: Many parents start around the second trimester, near 20 weeks. That gives you time to research items, compare options, and finish before a baby shower. Starting early also lets you add to the list gradually instead of rushing through every category in one stressful sitting.

faq.q: How many items should I put on a registry?
faq.a: There's no perfect number, but a balanced registry usually has a mix of small, medium, and large gifts so everyone can contribute at their budget. Focus on essentials first, then add nice-to-haves. Registering for more items than you expect gives guests plenty of choices.

faq.q: What baby items are not worth registering for?
faq.a: Skip single-use gadgets and items your baby may outgrow before using, like wipe warmers, specialty pillows, or shoes for newborns. Many parents find they don't need a changing table, full bottle warmer, or every accessory. Wait and buy these later only if you find you want them.

Yes, but lean toward larger sizes like 3 to 6 months, since newborns grow fast and often receive plenty of newborn outfits as gifts. Register for practical basics like onesies, sleepers, and seasonally appropriate layers rather than fancy outfits that may only be worn once.

faq.q: How do I choose between similar products?
faq.a: Compare safety standards, ease of cleaning, and how the item fits your space and routine. Read recent reviews and ask friends with babies what they actually used. When in doubt, register for the simpler option, since fewer features often means fewer things to break or clean.
